claims.text: The baseline TiVNbTa alloy is single-phase BCC, has approximately 800 MPa room-temperature yield strength and about 40% strain, and has approximately 330 MPa yield strength and 423 MPa compressive strength at 1273 K and 30% strain.
Substituting 5–10 at.% Mo into TiVNbTa will improve its high-temperature strength.
The Mo-modified alloy will retain approximately 40% room-temperature ductility.
The Mo addition will remain compatible with W and CuCrZr heat-transfer requirements.
Adding Mo to TiVNbTa forms a quaternary high-entropy alloy.
The Mo-modified TiVNbTa alloy will form a homogeneous single-phase BCC microstructure.
Mo addition will enhance lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening in TiVNbTa.
The enhanced lattice distortion will shift elevated-temperature deformation from screw-dominated to edge-dislocation-dominated slip.
Mo-induced lattice distortion lowers the activation energy for edge-dislocation motion.
A screw-to-edge dislocation-mode transition can produce a high-temperature strength plateau or improvement.
The modified alloy's yield strength at 1273 K will increase from approximately 330 MPa to 400–450 MPa.
Mo addition will not significantly impair the alloy's thermal conductivity.
Preserved thermal conductivity will permit effective heat transfer between W and CuCrZr.
The modification can avoid phase instability and excessive brittleness within the required operating-temperature range.
A minimum 20% increase in high-temperature yield strength is the specified performance criterion for the intervention.

contradictions.description: TiVNbTa already contains four elements, so adding Mo produces a five-element or quinary alloy, not the stated quaternary alloy.
